title: footprint.blast_radius 1.1.0
description: The export-surface diff of a footprint run: the exported symbols added, removed and signature-changed between the compared refs, each with the call sites of its name, and the changed files in languages that could not be analysed at all. Every symbol comes from graft's CLI contract `graft struct exports --json` (`graft.cli.struct_exports` 1.0.0); footprint derives the counts, the ordering, and the call sites. The call sites are footprint's own conservative whole-word identifier scan of the tracked files of the working tree -- no graft contract answers with a call site's line -- so they include the declaration itself and a mention in a comment, a string or prose, and they cannot see a call through dynamic dispatch or a re-export under another name. Each call site also names the system that contains it and carries a mitigation derived from reported facts alone, and exports.call_site_systems names the grouping rule, the mitigation derivation and every system with its call-site count. When graft is unavailable the exports section is stated as unavailable with a reason, never omitted, and the same holds for the scan. unanalysed_languages is independent of graft: it is present and empty when every changed file was in a supported language.

range.description: The git range compared, as given to git diff

available.description: False when graft could not be resolved, failed, or answered under a contract version footprint does not read

reason.description: Present when available is false: why the export surface could not be read

code.description: graft.not_resolved: no graft binary. graft.exports_failed: the subcommand exited non-zero. graft.output_unreadable: the answer was not JSON footprint could read. graft.schema_mismatch: a different _schema id or version. range.unresolved: the base of a three-dot range had no merge base.

detail.description: What happened, in enough words to act on

base.description: The base ref passed to graft: the merge base for a three-dot range, the given base otherwise

head.description: The head ref passed to graft

added.description: Exported symbols present at head and absent at base

removed.description: Exported symbols present at base and absent at head

signature_changed.description: Exported symbols present at both ends whose signature differs; each carries previous_signature when graft reported one

counts.description: The length of each list, so a reader needs no arithmetic; computed from the lists and nothing else

call_sites.description: Every symbol's call sites added up. Present only when the scan ran: a count of call sites nobody looked for is not a figure.

semver_impact.description: graft's own semver judgement for the surface change, passed through verbatim; null when graft reported none. footprint does not derive it.

call_site_scan.description: How the call sites on the symbols above were found, or why they were not. `method` is `identifier_scan`: every whole-word occurrence of the symbol's name in a tracked, non-binary file of the working tree, where a word character is a letter, a digit or an underscore in any script (`[\p{L}\p{N}_]`) on both sides -- `grep -w`'s own rule, which is what makes the independent grep oracle in footprint's test suite exact for an ASCII symbol name. When `available` is false no symbol carries `call_sites` at all, so a scan that did not run can never be read as one that found nothing.

files_skipped.description: Tracked files the scan did not match, each for a stated reason

binary.description: Files holding a NUL byte in their first 8192, skipped exactly as `grep -I` skips them

unreadable.description: Tracked files that could not be read, a file deleted from the working tree among them

reason.description: Present when available is false: why there are no call sites to show

code.description: scan.not_run: no scan was attached to this surface, so no tree was read. scan.ls_files_failed: `git ls-files -z` exited non-zero, so there was no file list to scan.

call_site_systems.description: How the call sites above group into systems, with the rule named on the record (flyingrobots/footprint#11). Present exactly when `call_site_scan.available` is true: a grouping of call sites nobody looked for is not a figure. The per-system `call_sites` counts sum to `counts.call_sites`, because every call site is in exactly one system, the unassigned group included.

rule.description: The grouping rule: a system is the first path segment of a call site's repository-relative path

rule_detail.description: The rule in words, so the output explains its own grouping without a reader fetching this schema

mitigation_rule.description: How every row's mitigation was derived, in words, for the same reason

unassigned.description: The group holding every call site in no system -- a file at the repository root. Named and listed last, never dropped.

systems.description: One entry per system holding at least one call site, ordered by name with the unassigned group last so the grouping follows the tree rather than the order the scan found the sites in

system.description: The first path segment, or "(unassigned)" for the call sites in no system

contract.description: The graft CLI contract that answered, so a reader knows which interface produced the list

allOf.description: A scan that ran lists every symbol's call sites, empty included: a symbol nothing references is never dropped, and the total is reported.
A scan that did not run carries no grouping at all, so an absent grouping can never be read as a change that reaches no system.

unanalysed_languages.description: Changed source files in languages footprint does not recognise as one graft's grammars can parse, grouped by extension with a count (flyingrobots/footprint#12). Present and empty when every changed file was in a supported language -- never omitted. Independent of exports.available: a parse failure in a supported language is never counted here, because this is extension-only and does not depend on whether graft ran or what it returned.

extension.description: The file extension, lowercase, dot included (e.g. ".hs"); "(none)" when the changed file's basename carries none

digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of range, exports and unanalysed_languages (spec §7.1)

symbol.description: The exported symbol's name, as graft reported it

file.description: The file the symbol is exported from, repository-relative

kind.description: graft's kind for the symbol (function, interface, field, export, ...); graft's vocabulary, not footprint's

signature.description: The signature at head, verbatim from graft, newlines and all

previous_signature.description: The signature at base, present only on a signature change graft reported one for

call_sites.description: Where the symbol's name occurs as a whole word in the tracked, non-binary files of the working tree, ordered by file then line, one entry per line however many times it occurs on that line. Each one names the system that contains it and carries its row's mitigation. Empty means the scan found none, which is reported rather than dropped; absent means no scan ran, which `call_site_scan.reason` states.

file.description: Repository-relative path, as `git ls-files` printed it

line.description: 1-based line number, as `grep -n` would print it

system.description: The system containing this call site: the first path segment of `file`, or "(unassigned)" when it has none (flyingrobots/footprint#11)

mitigation.description: This row's mitigation, derived from two reported facts and nothing else -- whether the call site is in the symbol's own declaring file, and what footprint's classification calls the file. Exactly one of three forms: the literal "None needed"; "Call site in <system>, outside the changed file."; or "Call site outside every known system, outside the changed file.". Never a judgement about importance, risk or coverage, and never advice: footprint reports and does not judge.

mitigation_basis.description: Which fact chose the mitigation, so the derivation is checkable from the record. declaring_file: the call site is in the very file the symbol is exported from. test_file: footprint's classification calls the call site's file a test. other_system: any other call site, inside a system. unassigned: any other call site, in no system. The first two are "None needed".
